entry.title: Coordinated “cyberattack” on Minnesota water utilities: What you need to know
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2021-22681, CVE-2023-3595, CVE-2024-6242

Iranian-affiliated CyberAv3ngers actors exploited CVE-2021-22681, a critical authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8) in internet-exposed Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens PLCs, to disrupt water systems across 30+ Minnesota communities in late July 2026; the vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild with no vendor patch available. The five-year-old vulnerability enables unauthenticated remote access through compromised cryptographic keys in engineering software; attackers modified PLC logic and disabled safety systems while manipulating HMI displays to prevent operator detection. Organizations must immediately disconnect internet-exposed PLCs, implement network segmentation isolating engineering workstations, enable physical mode switches set to "Run," deploy CIP Security, and maintain offline backups since architecture-level controls are the only remediation path. Ingest CISA AA26-097A indicators of compromise and monitor ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502, and 22 for connections from foreign hosting providers.

entry.title: Two Compromised joyfill npm Packages Run RAT When Imported Into Node.js
entry.content:
red-team · supply-chain-attack

Two npm packages in the @joyfill namespace (@joyfill/layouts@0.1.2-2773.beta.0 and @joyfill/components@4.0.0-rc24-2773-beta.4) have been compromised to deliver the DEV#POPPER remote access trojan, which executes malicious code at import time in Node.js environments. The attack employs encrypted payloads that are decrypted and executed during module initialization, providing attackers full system access. This threat is actively exploited in the wild as evidenced by the compromise of official package repositories. Immediately audit Node.js projects for these specific beta versions, remove affected packages, and restore from clean dependencies; consider implementing package pinning policies and monitoring for similar supply chain compromises in your dependency tree.

Exploitation appears active in the wild with targeting focused on China-based victims. The vulnerability has not been reported as actively exploited in the wild but poses severe risk due to the low privilege requirement for exploitation. Immediately upgrade to Gitea 1.27.1 or later, and review repository access controls to restrict write permissions where possible.

entry.title: @hypequery/clickhouse has SQL Injection in parameter escaping that allows arbitrary SQL execution (CVE-2026-54658)
entry.content:
vulnerability · sqli · CVE-2026-54658

The @hypequery/clickhouse npm package prior to version 2.0.2 contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability in the `escapeValue()` function used for parameter substitution. Attackers controlling parameter values can inject arbitrary SQL by exploiting improper escaping of trailing backslashes before closing quotes. There is no indication of active exploitation in the wild, but the critical severity warrants immediate action. Update to version 2.0.2 or later immediately, and audit applications using this package with user-controlled query parameters for potential compromise.

entry.title: Claude AI Just Cracked a Post-Quantum Test Scheme and Found a Faster 7-Round AES Attack
entry.content:
vulnerability · key-recovery

Claude AI discovered cryptanalytic attacks against post-quantum signature scheme HAWK-256 and seven-round AES-128, achieving 200-800x speedup improvements over prior methods. The HAWK attack exploits unused lattice symmetries while the AES attack demonstrates theoretical vulnerabilities in reduced-round variants. These are research findings against limited-round AES (not full AES) and a candidate post-quantum scheme; full AES-128 remains secure and is not exploited in the wild. Organizations should continue using full AES-128 and monitor HAWK's standardization status, as it may influence post-quantum cryptography selections, but no immediate patching is required for deployed systems.

entry.title: COFF Mixing - Hiding in Plain Sight
entry.content:
red-team · evasion

COFF Mixing describes a technique where adversaries weaponize Common Object File Format (COFF) binaries as an evasion method by leveraging legitimate COFF/BOF (Beacon Object File) runners to execute malicious code while evading detection. The technique exploits the flexibility of capability output formats (PIC/PICO/COFF) that require in-memory runners, making detection difficult since the malicious payload executes entirely in memory without touching disk. Severity is moderate-to-high as this is an active evasion technique observed in red team operations and likely exploited by advanced threat actors to bypass endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions. Organizations should implement memory scanning capabilities, monitor COFF loader execution, restrict access to legitimate COFF/BOF runners (such as those in Cobalt Strike), and enforce application whitelisting on development and administrative systems.

Read more · Source: rastamouse

entry.title: lettre has TLS hostname verification disabled when using Boring TLS backend (CVE-2026-46428)
entry.content:
vulnerability · tls-verification-bypass · CVE-2026-46428

The lettre email library's `boring-tls` backend contains a critical inverted-boolean bug that disables TLS hostname verification by default, allowing on-path attackers to intercept SMTP connections with any valid certificate regardless of domain. This affects only users with the `boring-tls` feature enabled; `native-tls` and `rustls` backends are unaffected. An attacker can capture credentials and message contents. Users should immediately upgrade to a patched version of lettre and consider switching to alternative TLS backends if immediate patching is unavailable.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: Poweradmin has Host Header Injection in OIDC redirect_uri, SAML ACS/SLO URL, and Logout Redirect Construction. (CVE-2026-54588)
entry.content:
vulnerability · host-header-injection · CVE-2026-54588

Poweradmin v4.3.2 is affected by a critical host header injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-54588) in OIDC redirect_uri, SAML ACS/SLO URLs, and logout redirect construction. An unauthenticated attacker can poison the HTTP_HOST header to redirect authorization codes to attacker-controlled servers, enabling account takeover without credentials. No evidence of in-the-wild exploitation is reported in the advisory. Immediate patching to a version addressing this vulnerability is critical; apply input validation on host headers and consider implementing host allowlisting as interim mitigation if patching is delayed.

entry.title: Over 24,000 exposed server BMCs leak password hash via decades-old flaw
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Over 24,000 internet-exposed servers are vulnerable to password hash disclosure through a two-decade-old flaw in their Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) interfaces. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to extract authentication credentials without requiring valid access, potentially enabling lateral movement and infrastructure compromise. The flaw appears actively exploited given the widespread exposure and age of the vulnerability. Organizations must immediately audit internet-facing BMCs, disable unnecessary network access, implement strong firewall rules restricting BMC connectivity, and apply available firmware patches to affected devices.

Iranian state-sponsored group Nimbus Manticore is deploying a novel Windows backdoor named NightLedger alongside custom WebSocket tunnelers to compromise targets across Middle East, Africa, and South Asia. The malware establishes persistence and converts victim systems into covert relay infrastructure for further network propagation. This represents an active, evolving threat with likely high severity given the actor's state backing and targeting scope. Organizations should enhance endpoint detection and response capabilities, implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement, and monitor for indicators of compromise associated with NightLedger and WebSocket tunneling traffic patterns.

entry.title: Critical OpenWrt DHCPv6 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
entry.content:
vulnerability · stack-overflow · CVE-2026-53921

OpenWrt's odhcpd DHCPv6 implementation contains a critical stack buffer overflow (CVE-2026-53921, CVSS 9.8) allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as root from the network. An attacker on the same network segment or with network access to the DHCPv6 service can trigger the flaw via malformed DHCPv6 packets. This vulnerability is actively exploitable and affects default OpenWrt configurations. Update to OpenWrt 24.10.8 or later immediately.

The vulnerability enabled unauthorized access and lateral movement within compromised networks. entry.title: Tengu Botnet Reboots Compromised Linux Devices When Defenders Kill Its Process
entry.content:
red-team · persistence,edr-evasion

Tengu is a Mirai-variant botnet targeting Linux devices through Telnet credential brute force attacks, notable for leveraging hardware watchdog timers to reboot compromised systems when security tools kill its process, enabling persistence mechanisms to re-establish infection. The botnet supports 25 DDoS attack variants and demonstrates moderate severity with active wild exploitation via credential attacks. Defend by disabling unnecessary hardware watchdog functionality, enforcing strong Telnet credentials or disabling Telnet entirely, implementing network segmentation to restrict brute-force attack surface, and deploying process monitoring with alert capabilities for botnet process termination attempts.

Read more · Source: thehackernews

entry.title: AutoIT Payload Injector , (Tue, Jul 28th)
entry.content:
red-team · payload-injection

AutoIT scripting language is being actively exploited by threat actors for payload injection into remote processes due to its ease of use and powerful capabilities. This technique leverages AutoIT's native functions to execute arbitrary code and maintain persistence, making it a favored tool in the malware ecosystem. The threat is HIGH severity given continued active exploitation in the wild by multiple threat actors. Mitigation should focus on restricting AutoIT script execution through application whitelisting, disabling unnecessary scripting engines, and monitoring for suspicious AutoIT process behavior and inter-process injection attempts.

entry.title: Researcher Says AI Helped Develop Linux Traffic-Control Race Into Root Exploit
entry.content:
vulnerability · use-after-free · CVE-2026-53264

A use-after-free race condition (CVE-2026-53264, CVSS 7.8) in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem allows local attackers to escalate privileges to root on affected systems, with the vulnerability reportedly discovered and exploited using AI-assisted techniques. The flaw affects CentOS Stream 9 and likely other distributions running vulnerable kernel versions, though no evidence of widespread wild exploitation has been reported. Users should apply kernel security patches from their distribution vendor as soon as they become available, and system administrators should restrict local user access where possible as a temporary mitigation. This case demonstrates AI's emerging role in both vulnerability discovery and exploit development, underscoring the need for rapid patching cycles.

entry.title: Helpdesk Hijackers: Teams Vishing, Quick Assist, and GoGRPC Backdoor
entry.content:
red-team · c2

This article details a sustained campaign by a likely initial access broker using Microsoft Teams vishing and Windows Quick Assist to compromise organizations since January 2026, deploying GoGRPC (a Go-based gRPC backdoor with four variants: Lep, Giver, Pet, and Kind) alongside supplementary tools including BlindDoor, RevSocket, PyGRPC, RSOX, and S3Siphon for reconnaissance, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. The threat actor has progressively increased operational sophistication, shifting from broad targeting to selective focus on corporate environments, with recent payloads utilizing more advanced obfuscation, TLS encryption, and environment-specific reconnaissance scripts. Severity is high given the confirmed ransomware group affiliation, active exploitation, and continuous tool evolution; recommended immediate actions include blocking identified C2 infrastructure, implementing email controls and authentication for Teams/Quick Assist access, training users on vishing tactics, hunting for GoGRPC and related indicators, and deploying behavioral detection for PowerShell-based staging and suspicious process execution patterns.

entry.title: Java Spring Boot "heapdump" scans, (Mon, Jul 27th)
entry.content:
vulnerability · information-disclosure

Spring Boot applications expose the "/actuator/heapdump" endpoint by default, which returns a binary memory dump (heapdump.hprof) containing the application's runtime state including sensitive data such as API keys, database credentials, and other secrets. This is a high-severity information disclosure vulnerability actively exploited in the wild through automated scanning. Organizations should immediately disable the heapdump endpoint in production environments by setting "management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude=heapdump" in application configuration, or restrict access to actuator endpoints through network controls and authentication mechanisms.

entry.content:
vulnerability · rce

A researcher disclosed a proof-of-concept for an authenticated RCE vulnerability in GitLab self-managed 18.11.3 and earlier versions that allows unprivileged users to execute arbitrary commands as the git user via a Jupyter notebook diff processing flaw. The vulnerability requires no admin rights or victim interaction, only the ability to commit code and trigger a diff comparison. This is a critical severity issue being exploited in the wild against unpatched instances. Administrators should immediately update to patched versions (18.11.4 or later, or 18.12.0+) and review recent commits for exploitation indicators.

entry.title: OpenAM: WebAuthn Java deserialization RCE via ObjectInputFilter depth>1 bypass (CVE-2026-62263)
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-62263

OpenAM's WebAuthn authentication module contains a Java deserialization remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-62263) where an incomplete ObjectInputFilter bypass allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by crafting malicious serialized objects with nested gadget chains. The filter only validates the root object at depth 1, leaving all nested classes unchecked. This is critical severity and requires immediate patching of affected org.openidentityplatform.openam:openam-auth-webauthn versions to implement proper depth-aware deserialization filtering or use a safer serialization mechanism.

entry.title: OpenAM: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Class.forName in AuthXMLUtils.createCustomCallback (CVE-2026-62379)
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-62379

OpenAM's AuthXMLUtils.createCustomCallback function contains a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-62379) in the `/authservice` authentication endpoint, which unsafely loads and instantiates arbitrary Java classes specified in XML input without validation. This pre-authentication flaw allows complete server compromise on default OpenAM configurations and affects openam-core. Immediate patching is required; if patches are unavailable, disable or restrict access to the `/authservice` endpoint at the network level pending vendor remediation.

entry.content:
vulnerability · sqli

Budibase's MySQL integration (npm/@budibase/server) contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability exploitable through the `multipleStatements: true` configuration, which allows attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands via user input and potentially compromise entire databases. This vulnerability is actively exploitable and likely being targeted in the wild given its critical severity rating. Immediate patching is required; disable `multipleStatements: true` in MySQL connection configurations as a temporary mitigation while awaiting the vendor security patch. Review application logs and database access patterns for signs of exploitation.

entry.title: Budibase: OIDC SSO account takeover: incoming identity linked by email without checking email_verified
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Budibase's OIDC SSO implementation (npm/@budibase/server) links incoming identities to existing accounts by email address alone without validating the OIDC `email_verified` claim, allowing account takeover. An attacker can create an OIDC identity with an unverified email matching a victim's Budibase account and gain full access to that account with all existing roles preserved. This is critical severity and exploitable in the wild. Upgrade Budibase immediately to a patched version that enforces `email_verified` validation before linking OIDC identities to existing accounts.

entry.title: Budibase: Unauthenticated REST Datasource Credential Theft via Cross-Origin Auth Leak
entry.content:
vulnerability · credential-theft

Budibase npm package prior to patched versions contains a critical vulnerability in REST datasource handling where stored credentials (Bearer tokens, Basic auth, static headers) are attached to outgoing requests before destination validation occurs. An attacker can redirect datasource queries to arbitrary hosts via absolute URLs or parameters, exfiltrating credentials to attacker-controlled servers; exploitation is trivial since queries can be published with PUBLIC role requiring no authentication. This vulnerability is likely being exploited given the ease of weaponization and public disclosure. Immediately update @budibase/server to the patched version and rotate all stored REST datasource credentials; review query configurations for suspicious host redirections.

entry.title: OpenDJ unauthenticated SSRF, local file read and unbounded-read DoS in the DSMLv2 gateway
entry.content:
vulnerability · ssrf

OpenDJ DSML-servlet versions through 5.1.1 contain a critical unauthenticated SSRF vulnerability in the DSMLv2 SOAP gateway that allows attackers to dereference arbitrary URIs without scheme validation or egress filtering. Attackers can exploit this to perform server-side request forgery against internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, read local files via file: URIs, and trigger unbounded-read denial of service attacks. The vulnerability is reachable by default without authentication and affects the opendj-dsml-servlet component. Immediate patching is required; upgrade to a version beyond 5.1.1 if available, or disable the DSMLv2 gateway and implement strict egress filtering and authentication controls as interim mitigation.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: OpenDJ SASL PLAIN authzid bypassing the proxy ACI scope check
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

OpenDJ's SASL PLAIN mechanism improperly validates proxy authorization requests by checking only the PROXIED_AUTH privilege while bypassing the mayProxy ACI scope check, allowing any account with proxied-auth privilege to assume any resolvable non-root identity. This vulnerability is critical as it circumvents access control restrictions that are properly enforced by all other proxy paths in OpenDJ. The issue affects org.openidentityplatform.opendj:opendj-server-legacy and should be patched immediately by upgrading to a patched version that validates both PROXIED_AUTH privilege and mayProxy ACI checks for SASL PLAIN authzid resolution.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: sm-crypto: Predictable SM2 key generation in Node.js: default RNG uses Math.random + wall clock
entry.content:
vulnerability · weak-rng

sm-crypto npm package (version 0.4.0) generates SM2 private keys and signing ephemeral scalars using an inadequate RNG that defaults to Math.random() and wall clock timing in Node.js environments because window.crypto.getRandomValues is unavailable. This critical vulnerability makes SM2 key generation predictable and allows recovery of private keys and forging of signatures. There is no evidence of active exploitation, but immediate patching is essential; users should upgrade to a patched version and consider regenerating any keys created with sm-crypto 0.4.0 in Node.js.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.content:
vulnerability · shell-injection

Shescape on Windows with CMD shell is vulnerable to shell injection via unescaped parentheses in the escape and escapeAll APIs, allowing attackers to break out of quoted contexts and execute arbitrary commands. The vulnerability affects users who explicitly configure the shell parameter to CMD or rely on CMD as the default shell. This is a critical severity issue that could enable unauthenticated remote code execution depending on how the library is used. Users should update to the patched version immediately and review any applications using Shescape with CMD shells to assess exposure.

entry.title: @better-auth/scim: account takeover and stale access via SCIM provider-id collision
entry.content:
vulnerability · account-takeover

@better-auth/scim plugin is vulnerable to account takeover and stale access token issues due to provider-ID collision. An authenticated attacker can generate SCIM tokens that allow them to assume control of other users' accounts or maintain access via stale tokens when custom provider IDs are reused across different authentication providers. The vulnerability is critical in severity and affects applications using the default `canGenerateToken` policy or custom policies that don't validate provider ID uniqueness. Users should immediately update @better-auth/scim to the patched version and audit their provider-ID configurations to ensure no collisions exist between SSO, SAML, OIDC, OAuth, and social authentication providers.

entry.title: Microsoft Kiota: Path/URL injection into generated Copilot plugin manifest via x-ai-* extensions (CVE-2026-59864)
entry.content:
vulnerability · path-injection · CVE-2026-59864

Microsoft Kiota's plugin generation (`kiota plugin add/generate`) fails to validate file paths from OpenAPI x-ai-* extensions, allowing attackers to inject path traversal sequences (../) or absolute paths into generated Copilot plugin manifests via `static_template.file` fields. This critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-59864) affects Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota and Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota.Builder NuGet packages and could enable unauthorized file access or plugin manipulation if exploited through compromised OpenAPI specifications. Organizations should immediately update affected Kiota packages and validate OpenAPI sources before processing them; implement input validation for file paths in generated manifests as defense-in-depth. No evidence of wild exploitation reported, but the attack surface is broad given reliance on external OpenAPI definitions.

Developers should immediately update to patched versions of nuget/Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota and nuget/Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota.Builder and avoid running `kiota info` against untrusted OpenAPI specifications.

entry.title: OpenSSL HollowByte Flaw Could Freeze Server Memory with 11-Byte TLS Requests
entry.content:
vulnerability · dos

OpenSSL versions prior to 1.1.1w, 3.0.x before 3.0.13, and 3.1.x before 3.1.1 are affected by the HollowByte denial-of-service vulnerability, which allows remote attackers to exhaust server memory by sending specially crafted 11-byte TLS requests that cause OpenSSL to allocate up to 131 KB per request without proper cleanup. The flaw is a memory exhaustion issue that can freeze or degrade server performance on glibc systems, and allocated memory persists until process restart. No known active exploitation has been reported; however, the fix was silently deployed in June without CVE assignment or security advisory. Immediately patch to OpenSSL 1.1.1w, 3.0.13, or 3.1.1 or later, and monitor servers for suspicious TLS connection patterns prior to patching.

entry.content:

entry.content:

MantisBT versions 2.28.3 and earlier contain critical reflected XSS vulnerabilities in `/admin/install.php` where user-supplied parameters are echoed unescaped via printf format strings, requiring no authentication. The existing Content Security Policy lacks a form-action directive, enabling attackers to inject credential-phishing forms and open redirects despite script-src restrictions. This vulnerability is actively exploitable for credential theft and other attacks. Upgrade to MantisBT 2.28.4 or later immediately, or implement strict input validation and additional CSP directives (form-action 'self') as interim mitigation.
